patterns.note: Full-screen background color transitions smoothly between bold, saturated hues as the user scrolls down the page, acting as a visual separator for content states.

The primary content (age gate question and options) remains visually fixed in the viewport while the background color changes and the page content scrolls underneath, creating a layered effect where foreground elements adapt their color for contrast.
The initial page content is centrally aligned and minimal, featuring a single interactive element, contrasting with a multi-column, text-heavy footer that appears after scrolling.
Prominent use of a large, bold sans-serif typeface for key interactive elements, with smaller, lighter sans-serif for secondary navigation and information in the footer.

technique_notes: The site uses a scroll-triggered animation system (likely locomotive-scroll) where the background color of the main content area changes dynamically based on scroll position. The foreground content (age gate text and icon) maintains a fixed position relative to the viewport, while its color adapts for contrast against the changing background.

Sections are revealed by scrolling, with the background color acting as a strong visual separator and transition between different content states or sections, rather than traditional section dividers.

design_tokens.type_scale: Large, bold sans-serif for primary interactive elements (~3-4x body text), with smaller, regular sans-serif for navigation and informational text.
design_tokens.radius: Sharp, with no visible rounded corners on elements or containers.
design_tokens.spacing: Very airy for the initial age gate, transitioning to a balanced density for the footer content with clear vertical rhythm.

standout: The most distinctive feature is the full-screen, scroll-triggered background color transitions that dynamically adapt to the content, creating a highly immersive and interactive initial experience. The age gate itself is presented as a persistent, adapting overlay rather than a modal, making it feel integrated with the page's scroll journey.
